name: Vegetarian Drunken Noodles
steps: Gently separate fresh wide rice noodles with oiled fingers. Press and cube tofu, slice chilies and pepper, halve baby corn and wash basil leaves. Whisk light and dark soy sauces with vegetarian mushroom sauce, sugar and measured 35 ml water.
Heat 20 ml oil in a wide wok over high heat. Sear tofu cubes 2–3 minutes on each side until golden; remove. Do not crowd the pan or they will steam instead of brown.
Add remaining 25 ml oil. Stir-fry garlic and sliced red chilies for about 20 seconds until fragrant without burning. Add pepper and baby corn and toss for 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.

Add broad rice noodles and let them touch the hot wok for 30–45 seconds to pick up a little char. Pour in the prepared sauce and return tofu. Lift and toss carefully for 2–3 minutes until the noodles are hot and evenly glazed.

Switch off the heat. Add holy basil and toss just until leaves wilt from the residual heat; prolonged cooking dulls their aroma. Divide among four plates and serve immediately while the noodles are springy.
tips: Check mushroom sauce for a vegetarian label; ordinary oyster sauce and fish sauce are unsuitable. The reviewed photo shows wide rice noodles, red chilies, basil, green pepper, baby corn and browned tofu.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
